results.title: Validation is the central challenge for generative social simulation
results.content: # Validation is the central challenge for generative social simulation: a critical review of LLMs in agent-based modeling. The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs)—which can generate fluent, context-aware natural language, mimic human reasoning, and exhibit goal-directed behavior—has led researchers to explore their integration into ABMs. This new class of models, often referred to as “Generative ABMs” (GABMs) or “generative social simulation”, leverages LLMs to simulate human-like agents who can plan, reason, and interact via language (Törnberg et al. These capabilities were first demonstrated in a 2023 study that used LLMs to simulate human behavior in a Sims-like virtual environment, where generative agents began to exhibit human-like behavior and complex social dynamics (Park et al. Mou X, Ding X, He Q, Wang L, Liang J, Zhang X, Sun L, Lin J, Zhou J, Huang X, et al (2024a) From individual to society: A survey on social simulation driven by large language model-based agents.

results.title: LLMs for Social Simulation: Advancements and Challenges - Medium
results.content: Since “Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior” (Park et al., 2023) showed that LLM-driven agents in a sandbox world could exhibit emergent social behaviors, research on Large Language Model (LLM) social simulation has bifurcated into two distinct streams: one demonstrating the ability of synthetic agents to emulate human personality and behavior, the other critically examining the validity and limitations of such simulations. When provided with detailed backstories (persona prompting), LLMs can accurately reproduce the survey distributions of specific human demographics (e.g., voting patterns of US voters), effectively allowing for “silicon sampling” (Argyle et al., 2023). Moving beyond zero-shot prompting, fine-tuning models on actual social science datasets significantly boosts their ability to predict human behavior, suggesting that “superficial” simulation can be deepened with better data (Kolluri et al., 2025). *Using large language models to simulate multiple humans and replicate human subject studies.* Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML).

A Critical Review of Generative Social Simulations, by Maik Larooij and 1 other authors. > Abstract:Recent advancements in AI have reinvigorated Agent-Based Models (ABMs), as the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to the emergence of ``generative ABMs'' as a novel approach to simulating social systems. While ABMs offer means to bridge micro-level interactions with macro-level patterns, they have long faced criticisms from social scientists, pointing to e.g., lack of realism, computational complexity, and challenges of calibrating and validating against empirical data. This paper reviews the generative ABM literature to assess how this new approach adequately addresses these long-standing criticisms. |  | (or  arXiv:2504.03274v1 [cs.MA] for this version) |.
